new_results.statement: For rank-two physical rows with determinant volume law p and disjointness probability delta>0, the translated two-dimensional product Fourier integral is at most 16*pi^2*(E2*delta)^(-1/2).

In the exact angular-cancellation one-sided packet, ||p_Q||inf <=12 e^(1/3) s_3(A)^(-1) delta^(-1/3); the density is continuous C0 in this branch; the half-Riesz copy-time integral is <=(48/5)sqrt(pi)e^(1/6)s_3(A)^(-1/2)delta^(-1/6).

For any probability law on two-sets with iid disjointness probability delta, either a vertex incidence is >=1-delta-(3/2)^(1/3)delta^(1/3), or a triple carries at least the same edge mass. For determinant volume sampling this is a near-coloop OR near-three-coordinate alternative.

unresolved_implication: Pay the near-coloop and near-three-coordinate collars uniformly as delta->0 using product-preserving exact-coloop/grouped-hub/finite-coordinate mechanisms; do not select one fragile minor or use conditional sum/difference caps.
